messages:
Priya: Heads up everyone: next week weegin the Org Permissions & Service Account migration. Goal: retire embedded PATs, move service-auth to GitHub Apps + SCIM for Jira users, and harmonize org roles. Migration doc: https://go/redwood/org-auth-migration (please review)

Tom: Timeline? Will this affect deploys or builds?

Priya: Rolling canary Mon-Wed; org-wide enforcement Fri. No planned downtime, but expect CI job failures for repos that still use PATs. We'll post failing repo list in the doc.

Jules: What about bots that call Jira APIs? We have a couple of internal agents using basic auth.

Infra-Chris: For Jira bots we
re creating a Jira Service App that issues scoped API keys via our secret broker. We'll run a compatibility layer for 30 days for critical flows. Please add any bot names to the spreadsheet in the doc.

Eli: SCIM provisioning changes sound disruptive for HR-managed groups. Any perms changes to the "engineering" org team?

Priya: SCIM only for user sync; group-to-org mapping will be stable. We will, however, remove the legacy "write:all" team permission and replace with role-based teams (maintainer, contributor). Owners will get a 7-day heads-up to review team mappings.

engbot: Migration checklist created: https://go/redwood/checklists/org-auth-migration. Add repos or apps by commenting `add: <name>` on the checklist.

Tom: How do we migrate Service Accounts that run long-lived cron jobs on GCE and k8s? They currently embed PATs in k8s secrets.

Infra-Chris: Plan: rotate the k8s secrets to reference Vault-backed tokens. We'll push a small init container to refresh tokens at pod start and a cronjob to refresh for long-lived replicas. Example snippet in the doc:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: deploy-bot-creds
stringData:
  token: "{{ from_vault \"secret/data/ci/deploy-bot\" }}"
```

Nina: Any changes for local dev? People push to feature branches that trigger GitHub Actions that read secrets.

Priya: Locally, devs should install the new `rbac-migrator` CLI or `vault-auth-helper` and run `vault-auth-helper login`. We'll add a short guide to the developer handbook and a dotfiles template.

Eli: Are we enabling GitHub Apps at org-level now? Some repos have custom permissions for apps; will they be auto-granted?

Priya: We will enable the org GitHub App but it will request repo access only for repos that opt-in via the checklist. We will not auto-grant access to all repos. Repo maintainers will approve through the normal OAuth flow.

Jules: Please ensure audit logs include the mapping from old PAT to new app/token for troubleshooting.

Priya: Agreed. Audit entries will record migration actions. Security will redact token values but keep request IDs. If you need a mapping to debug, open a security ticket.

Tom: Exceptions? We have a compliance-bound customer repo that can't use external brokers.

Priya: There's an exceptions process in the doc. For air-gapped or restricted repos we have an on-prem agent option; submit the request by Apr 10. Approval required by Security + Infra.

Infra-Chris: Ops note: we'll run a dry-run job on Wed night that lists repos which will break. Watch the repo list and ping me if you're on-call.

Nina: Can we get a simple diagnostic command to check a repo's readiness?

Priya: Yes: `./scripts/check-auth-readiness.sh <repo>` will be added to the repo template. It returns PASS/FAIL and a small remediation hint.

Eli: Thx. I'll add our customer-facing repos to the checklist and coordinate with product.

Priya: Thanks team. Action items: add entries to checklist, run readiness script, owners review team mappings, file exceptions by Apr 10. I'll post a follow-up with the canary list tomorrow.

engbot: Migration scheduled: canary Mon Apr 11; enforcement Fri Apr 15. Next status update Tue 09:00 PDT.
